assessments.reasoning: The first three paragraphs on printed p. vii directly connect the publisher’s named FOCAL-8 service program with the FOCAL language, then describe the manual’s treatment of the commands that constitute that language.

challenge.method: Challenged the direction and granularity of the relation by reading the full preface and comparing the 1968 opening convention, the 1970 shorthand, and the later preface references to QUAD and LIBRA.
challenge.results: The document names the program and its language in the same passage. A directed association from FOCAL language to the identified FOCAL-8 program matches the evidence. Shared shorthand supplies no general alias or equivalence claim.

limitations: This is the relationship documented in the January 1970 printing. Binary identity, other FOCAL implementations, descendant portability, and compatibility require independent sources.
